text:
Mia: heads up — saw a ~9% drop in leading-token prefix-cache hits on canary after the quantization scheduler + kernel-tilt rollout this morning :thinking_face:
Raj: ugh, can you paste the metric window? which model and which kernel variant?
Mia: model: redwood-open-1.2; kernel: matmul-tilt-v2 + quant-sched=aggressive; window: 04:00-06:30 UTC; prefix_hit_rate went from 86% -> 77% on tail QPS (p50 p95 stable)
Elena: did you check if the key normalization changed? thats often the silent one after kernel swaps
Mia: did a quick diff, tokenization unchanged. suspecting early-KV-hash noise — warmup traces show more distinct keys for the same prompt fingerprints
Sam: can you dump a few examples? even obfuscated prompts to check suffix/prefix alignment
Mia: pasted 3 examples below (obfuscated):
```
seed: 0x7a3f
prompt_fingerprint: 0x9b11 -> pre-rollup keys: [0x9b11-0x01] after-rollout keys: [0x9b11-0x7c] (different salt)
```
Mia: also ran quick perf profile: noticed extra memcpy in kv-serialize path when tiling is enabled
Raj: memcpy? that smells like a kernel ABI path that toggles a fallback serializer. which build-id?
Mia: build: rwd-runtime-2026.03.10-tilt. compile flags: -DUSE_TILED_ATTENTION, quant profile: q8aggr
Elena: could be quant scheduler inserting a rehash step to adapt placement. check code path in kv_cache::serialize — we added a conditional for alignment in the last PR
Sam: pinging @luca-bot to spin a repro on canary with tracing enabled (kv keys + trace_id)
luca-bot: repro job launched: rwd-repro-4160001200; nodes: canary-2a/2b; tracing-level: kv_keys, mem_events; ETA ~12m
Mia: added a couple of quick graphs: prefix_hit_rate (p50 request streams) + distinct_key_count per minute. distinct_key_count jumped 11% at rollout time
Raj: 11% more distinct keys -> explains hit rate drop. but why did distinct keys change if inputs same? maybe kernel changed padding/ordering when serializing KV cache
Elena: check for token-level padding or a change in PRNG for salt: e.g., using stack uninitialized memory as part of key when tiling reorders buffers
Sam: steps to reproduce locally?
Mia: quick script I used:
```
# reproduce locally (obfuscated)
python tools/repro_prefix_keys.py --model redwood-open-1.2 --kernel matmul-tilt-v2 --quant q8aggr --traces out.json
```
Mia: attaching minimal out.json snippet (inline): distinct_keys: [0x9b11,0x9b12,0x9b7c] where 0x9b7c only appears after rollout
Raj: I'll grep the kernel ABI wrapper for any uninitialized fields used in key build. if found, we should gate the tiling flag for the KV path
Elena: also check fastpath vs fallback in serializer — we added a small optimization to avoid copies which might change the ordering of appended bytes
Sam: if it's ordering we can canonicalize key: hash(normalize(prefix) + length + stable-salt) as a short-term mitigation (cheap)
Mia: agree. mitigation proposal: add a canonicalization shim in KV lookup to mask ordering changes and roll a canary with shim on for 24h
Raj: can we instead revert the quant-scheduler flag for canary while we diagnose? low-risk toggle available?
Mia: yes, quant-sched=aggressive is a feature-flag. I can flip to conservative on canary in 5m and monitor hit-rate
Sam: prefer quick canonicalization + metric check. revert is heavier for rollout but keep as fallback
Elena: also run a binary diff of serializer between builds: rwd-runtime-2026.03.08 (good) vs 2026.03.10 (bad). I'll start that now
Mia: action items: 1) Mia toggle quant-sched on canary -> conservative (in 5m) 2) Raj grep kernel ABI + serializer 3) Elena run binary diff + hunt for ordering changes 4) Sam implement canonicalization shim (small PR) 5) Luca keep repro running and post trace artifacts
Raj: noted. if grep shows uninitialized memory, hotfix with zeroing asap
Sam: i'll open PR for shim with tests to assert stable key generation across kernel variants
Mia: thanks all — will post results in thread. current hit-rate backfill window saved as snapshot: snap-4160001234
Elena: quick note — if canonicalization reduces hit-rate variance but adds CPU, quantify cost. don't trade 10% hit for 15% CPU increase without costing model units
Mia: good point. will run small perf sweep after shim PR
luca-bot: repro job completed; artifacts uploaded to s3://rwd-repro/4160001234/trace.tar.gz
Raj: found suspicious memset omission in tiled_serializer.cpp: around line ~214 it used memcpy from misaligned src, leaving tail bytes uninitialized when length % 8 != 0
Mia: can you patch to explicit zero tail and run canary test?
Raj: will patch and deploy to canary build + update quant-sched back to aggressive to see if hit-rate recovers
Sam: if patch + zeroing fixes, we can ship micro-patch and keep quant-sched. otherwise revert quant-sched flag
Mia: posting interim numbers: after Raj's zero-tail patch + redeploy on canary, prefix_hit_rate climbed to 85% (from 77%), distinct_key_count dropped back ~9%
Elena: nice. that suggests ordering/garbage bytes were the root cause
Mia: will prepare a short postmortem + recommend test: add deterministic-key-unit test to CI to catch this class of bug (serialize -> roundtrip -> stable hash across kernels)
Sam: agree. I'll add CI test and a perf guard.
Mia: closing here for now. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
_reserved_note: No title field per agents.md. All messages are one continuous string with sender prefixes.
